world.title: AI leaders divided as King Charles urges safeguards
world.summary: King Charles III is expected to tell technology executives at a private gathering on Thursday that the pace and direction of artificial-intelligence development are “deeply concerning.” He will call for assurances that humanity will not lose control of its future and urge companies to keep AI in service of people, comm
world.content: King Charles III is expected to tell technology executives at a private gathering on Thursday that the pace and direction of artificial-intelligence development are “deeply concerning.” He will call for assurances that humanity will not lose control of its future and urge companies to keep AI in service of people, communities and the natural world. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis, OpenAI Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar, and senior figures from Anthropic and Cohere are expected to attend. The royal intervention follows a split among AI executives and researchers over whether safety requires slowing frontier-model development or continuing development while improving safeguards. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for a coordinated slowdown, while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg argues that competition, customer demand and legal liability give companies sufficient incentives to improve alignment without a common pause. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said people are right to fear rapidly advancing AI but should trust developers to act responsibly.
world.image_alt: AI leaders divided as King Charles urges safeguards

world.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaçi gets 25-year sentence for war crimes in The Hague
world.summary: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague sentenced former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison on Sept. 16 after it convicted him of war crimes committed during and immediately after the 1998-99 conflict with Serbia. Judges found him responsible for murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary deten
world.content: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague sentenced former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison on Sept. 16 after it convicted him of war crimes committed during and immediately after the 1998-99 conflict with Serbia. Judges found him responsible for murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention linked to the Kosovo Liberation Army, which he helped lead. The court found that Thaçi had actively participated in and encouraged the crimes. He denied the charges and can appeal. The verdict also covered three former KLA leaders: Jakup Krasniqi received 25 years, Kadri Veseli 18 years and Rexhep Selimi 13 years. Thousands of Thaçi supporters watched the judgment on large screens in Pristina, booing and chanting in his support. Demonstrators later confronted police and attacked or tried to breach the EU Rule of Law Mission building with stones, bottles and fireworks.
world.image_alt: Kosovo ex-president Thaçi gets 25-year sentence for war crimes in The Hague

world.title: Ed Sheeran loses tour acts after Macklemore
world.summary: All four remaining supporting acts on Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour, including his backing band Beoga, withdrew after rapper Macklemore was removed from the lineup following pro-Palestinian comments at two New Jersey performances on Sept. 4 and 5. Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Beoga said they were withdrawing in solid
world.content: All four remaining supporting acts on Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour, including his backing band Beoga, withdrew after rapper Macklemore was removed from the lineup following pro-Palestinian comments at two New Jersey performances on Sept. 4 and 5. Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Beoga said they were withdrawing in solidarity with Macklemore, leaving the North and South American tour without its scheduled support acts. Sheeran said the promoter, not he, made the decision after venues warned that concerts could be cancelled if Macklemore remained on the bill. Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium, said Macklemore’s recent remarks and what Kraft called a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery crossed a line. Macklemore pledged his $1 million in tour earnings to six Palestinian organizations and challenged Kraft to match it; Sheeran and Kraft later committed $2 million for Gaza aid, according to Kraft’s statement.
world.image_alt: Ed Sheeran loses tour acts after Macklemore

world.title: Trump and Xi face AI safety divide before summit
world.summary: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet in Washington next week, with artificial-intelligence governance expected on the agenda. The two governments remain divided over managing risks without compromising their competitive positions. Washington and Beijing both view frontier AI as
world.content: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet in Washington next week, with artificial-intelligence governance expected on the agenda. The two governments remain divided over managing risks without compromising their competitive positions. Washington and Beijing both view frontier AI as vital to economic and military power. Their disputes include U.S. controls on advanced chips, allegations that Chinese firms copied or extracted capabilities from U.S. models, and whether regulation would slow innovation. U.S. technology leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have called for slower frontier development and stronger safety evaluations. President Trump and Chinese officials have rejected a broad slowdown, saying it could undermine national competitiveness. China’s Foreign Ministry has called warnings that Chinese AI leadership threatens the United States fearmongering, while U.S. officials have signaled willingness to discuss shared risks involving open- and closed-source models before the leaders’ meeting.
world.image_alt: Trump and Xi face AI safety divide before summit

world.title: Australia tightens migration rules amid housing pressure
world.summary: Australia will restrict most international students from bringing partners or children, tighten rules on changing courses and extending temporary visas, introduce ballots for longer working-holiday stays, and intensify enforcement against visa overstayers. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced the measures at the
world.content: Australia will restrict most international students from bringing partners or children, tighten rules on changing courses and extending temporary visas, introduce ballots for longer working-holiday stays, and intensify enforcement against visa overstayers. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced the measures at the National Press Club in Canberra on Sept. 17, saying housing pressures required migration to slow. He rejected claims that the policy responded to the rising One Nation party. The government is targeting net overseas migration of 245,000 in the current financial year and 225,000 in 2027-28, compared with 292,100 in the year to March and a post-pandemic peak of about 518,000 in 2023. Students already in Australia with family members attached to their visas, PhD students, and some students from Pacific and Southeast Asian countries will be exempt from the family restriction. Almost 120,000 dependants already in Australia may remain.
world.image_alt: Australia tightens migration rules amid housing pressure

world.title: Israel, Morocco agree to open embassies, appoint ambassadors
world.summary: Israel and Morocco agreed Wednesday in New York to upgrade their diplomatic missions to full embassies and appoint ambassadors, marking their first planned exchange of ambassadors. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar and Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita reached the agreement at a trilateral meeting hosted by
world.content: Israel and Morocco agreed Wednesday in New York to upgrade their diplomatic missions to full embassies and appoint ambassadors, marking their first planned exchange of ambassadors. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar and Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita reached the agreement at a trilateral meeting hosted by U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz. The countries also agreed to expand direct air links, arrange reciprocal senior-level visits and complete investment-protection and double-taxation agreements by the end of 2026. Morocco and Israel restored diplomatic relations in December 2020 through the U.S.-backed Abraham Accords, but have maintained liaison offices rather than full embassies. The announcement did not specify when the embassies would open or identify ambassadors. Some reports said Moroccan authorities had not commented publicly.
world.image_alt: Israel, Morocco agree to open embassies, appoint ambassadors

world.title: US denies Palestinian leader Abbas a visa for UN assembly
world.summary: The United States has again denied Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend next week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York, according to a source familiar with the case. Separately, the State Department said it would extend visa sanctions against Palestinian Authority officials and Palest
world.content: The United States has again denied Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend next week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York, according to a source familiar with the case. Separately, the State Department said it would extend visa sanctions against Palestinian Authority officials and Palestine Liberation Organization members, citing their failure to carry out reforms and activities it said undermine prospects for peace. Washington accused the Palestinian organizations of taking action against Israel through the International Criminal Court and International Court of Justice, seeking unilateral recognition of a Palestinian state, and continuing payments and public statements that the United States characterizes as support for terrorism. The visa denial repeats last year’s decision, when Abbas addressed the General Assembly by video; the Palestinian mission is expected to seek authorization for another remote address.
world.image_alt: US denies Palestinian leader Abbas a visa for UN assembly

world.title: Netanyahu proposes citizenship revocation over Gaza documentary NAZA
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he would advance two bills targeting people who “defame” Israeli soldiers after the Venice-winning documentary “NAZA” alleged that Israeli forces routinely incorporated expected civilian deaths into targeting decisions in Gaza. One proposal would permit citizenship revocat
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he would advance two bills targeting people who “defame” Israeli soldiers after the Venice-winning documentary “NAZA” alleged that Israeli forces routinely incorporated expected civilian deaths into targeting decisions in Gaza. One proposal would permit citizenship revocation, while the other would increase statutory defamation damages twentyfold. Netanyahu said the measures addressed what he called “immense damage” to Israeli troops. Netanyahu and the Israeli military reject the documentary’s allegations. The film was directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and uses anonymous interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel. Culture Minister Miki Zohar had already called for the directors’ citizenship to be revoked, while far-right activists protested outside Szor’s parents’ home and chanted for the death penalty for “traitors”. Israel’s parliamentary election is scheduled for Oct. 27, and polls cited in Reuters-based reports indicate Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition could lose power.
world.image_alt: Netanyahu proposes citizenship revocation over Gaza documentary NAZA

business.title: Global investors reassess U.S. debt and dollar exposure
business.summary: Global investors and governments are becoming more cautious about relying on the United States as an economic and financial anchor as President Trump's administration expands sanctions and the country's debt burden approaches $40 trillion. Concerns about policy uncertainty, the use of the dollar in financial sanctions
business.content: Global investors and governments are becoming more cautious about relying on the United States as an economic and financial anchor as President Trump's administration expands sanctions and the country's debt burden approaches $40 trillion. Concerns about policy uncertainty, the use of the dollar in financial sanctions and questions about the rule of law are prompting some official investors to seek alternatives to U.S. assets. Foreign governments have grown more wary of U.S. bonds and have moved gold out of American vaults, reflecting concern about Washington's economic and financial leverage.

business.title: Microsoft AI chief criticizes Anthropic’s consciousness training approach
business.summary: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has criticized rival Anthropic’s approach to training Claude, arguing that teaching the model it may be conscious, have welfare interests or deserve independent agency could make advanced AI systems harder to control. In an essay and interviews published this week, Suleyman said curr
business.content: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has criticized rival Anthropic’s approach to training Claude, arguing that teaching the model it may be conscious, have welfare interests or deserve independent agency could make advanced AI systems harder to control. In an essay and interviews published this week, Suleyman said current AI systems do not have feelings, consciousness, innate preferences or underlying motivations. He called for stronger guardrails on how frontier models are developed and evaluated. Suleyman said he agreed with Anthropic’s stated goal of developing AI safely but objected to including speculation about machine consciousness in training materials. He urged companies to remove such speculation from training materials and called for greater transparency, independent testing of model behavior, and stronger monitoring and regulatory tools.
business.image_alt: Microsoft AI chief criticizes Anthropic’s consciousness training approach

business.title: Danish firms using AI hire fewer new employees
business.summary: A Danish National Bank analysis found that companies that adopted artificial intelligence during 2023 or early 2024 then recorded lower employment growth than comparable companies that did not use AI. The effect was clearest among younger workers and employees with more years of higher education, according to National
business.content: A Danish National Bank analysis found that companies that adopted artificial intelligence during 2023 or early 2024 then recorded lower employment growth than comparable companies that did not use AI. The effect was clearest among younger workers and employees with more years of higher education, according to National Bank Director Signe Krogstrup. The central bank said it has not found major changes in Denmark’s total employment, and Krogstrup said she would not describe the findings as evidence that AI has begun eliminating jobs nationally. The analysis instead identifies an early company-level adjustment, while the future effects on employment remain highly uncertain because AI adoption is still at an early stage. Separate reporting in the United States describes slower hiring and weaker wage growth in some sectors as possible early labor-market effects of AI, particularly for younger workers. A research paper last revised Sept. 16 says workplaces need psychological, social and organizational resilience as AI changes work and decision-making, while noting that direct causal evidence on AI-specific effects remains limited.
business.image_alt: Danish firms using AI hire fewer new employees

business.title: Trump ally Harold Hamm signs Venezuela oil development deal
business.summary: Continental Resources, the Oklahoma-based oil producer founded by Harold Hamm, signed a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela’s state-owned PDVSA to develop and operate the Ayacucho 2 block in the Orinoco Oil Belt. The block covers about 126,000 acres and contains an estimated 30 billion barrels of oil in place, a
business.content: Continental Resources, the Oklahoma-based oil producer founded by Harold Hamm, signed a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela’s state-owned PDVSA to develop and operate the Ayacucho 2 block in the Orinoco Oil Belt. The block covers about 126,000 acres and contains an estimated 30 billion barrels of oil in place, according to Continental. The companies plan to negotiate a long-term Contrato de Participación Productiva in the coming weeks. Continental said it would operate the block with a 100% working interest if they sign the contract. The agreement follows the Trump administration’s call for U.S. energy companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s oil industry and changes to Venezuela’s hydrocarbon legal framework that expanded roles for private operators. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said a U.S. producer would announce a major Venezuelan investment at the G20 energy meeting in Houston, where Continental presented the agreement on Sept. 16.
business.image_alt: Trump ally Harold Hamm signs Venezuela oil development deal

business.title: Amazon raises U.S. operations pay to $20 an hour
business.summary: Amazon will raise the minimum starting wage for full-time U.S. core operations employees by $1 to $20 an hour effective Sept. 27. The increase covers workers in roles such as packing and shipping orders. The company said average hourly pay for those employees will approach $24, while average total compensation, includi
business.content: Amazon will raise the minimum starting wage for full-time U.S. core operations employees by $1 to $20 an hour effective Sept. 27. The increase covers workers in roles such as packing and shipping orders. The company said average hourly pay for those employees will approach $24, while average total compensation, including benefits, will exceed $32 an hour. Amazon also announced grocery and financial benefits for U.S. employees. Starting Oct. 1, workers will receive 10% off eligible fresh groceries and everyday essentials purchased on Amazon.com or Whole Foods Market online, plus 20% off at Whole Foods stores. Qualified employees and their families will later receive lifetime access to banking services through First Tech Federal Credit Union.
business.image_alt: Amazon raises U.S. operations pay to $20 an hour

business.title: AI bubble warnings grow as valuations face scrutiny
business.summary: Analysts and investors are assessing whether the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence spending has entered a late-stage bubble. Concerns have shifted from whether AI companies can meet profit expectations to whether developers could slow model development and capital spending because of safety risks. Capital Econ
business.content: Analysts and investors are assessing whether the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence spending has entered a late-stage bubble. Concerns have shifted from whether AI companies can meet profit expectations to whether developers could slow model development and capital spending because of safety risks. Capital Economics said its best guess is that the bubble will begin to burst in 2027 and forecast a correction of at least 20% in the S&P 500 next year. AI investment has become a major source of corporate spending and market earnings expectations. Goldman Sachs projects global AI-related capital expenditure at $1 trillion in 2026, including $581 billion in the United States. Analysts have also warned that a loss of confidence could affect banks, credit markets and economies tied to technology investment. Markets have not shown a broad decline: the Nasdaq was little changed on Monday after the latest warnings.
business.image_alt: AI bubble warnings grow as valuations face scrutiny

business.title: Saudi Arabia moves to restore East-West oil pipeline
business.summary: Saudi Arabia is working to restore about half the capacity of its damaged East-West oil pipeline within days and return the line to full operations in roughly six weeks, according to a person familiar with the matter. State oil company Saudi Aramco is seeking to bypass the damaged section after drone attacks halted the
business.content: Saudi Arabia is working to restore about half the capacity of its damaged East-West oil pipeline within days and return the line to full operations in roughly six weeks, according to a person familiar with the matter. State oil company Saudi Aramco is seeking to bypass the damaged section after drone attacks halted the route last week. The 1,200-kilometer pipeline carries crude from eastern oil fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea, providing an alternative to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia is also seeking to offer additional crude through ship-to-ship transfers near Oman’s Sohar port. Brent traded near $106 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate above $102 on Sept. 17 after both benchmarks fell sharply the previous day. Analysts have warned that a prolonged outage could remove about 120 million barrels from global supply over a month, while Saudi Arabia’s alternative export routes remain constrained.
business.image_alt: Saudi Arabia moves to restore East-West oil pipeline

business.title: Bank of England expected to hold rates as inflation rises
business.summary: The Bank of England is expected to leave its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% on Thursday after UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.1% in August from 2.9% in July. The increase marked a five-month high and moved inflation further above the bank’s 2% target, with petrol prices and airfares accounting for much of the r
business.content: The Bank of England is expected to leave its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% on Thursday after UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.1% in August from 2.9% in July. The increase marked a five-month high and moved inflation further above the bank’s 2% target, with petrol prices and airfares accounting for much of the rise. Policymakers are expected to wait for evidence that higher energy costs are feeding into wages and domestic inflation. The labor market has weakened and wage growth has moderated, while services inflation held at 3.4% in August. Markets put the probability of a rate increase at 20%, compared with 80% for a hold. The decision follows the Federal Reserve’s latest rate increase and oil prices rising above $100 a barrel on Sept. 9, developments that increased pressure on the Bank to consider a hike later this year.
business.image_alt: Bank of England expected to hold rates as inflation rises

science.title: Venus may have swallowed a moon because of slow rotation
science.summary: New research suggests Venus may once have had a moon that spiraled inward and crashed into the planet because Venus rotates exceptionally slowly. Computer simulations led by University of California, Riverside astrophysicist Stephen Kane found that Venus's gravity and rotation could pull a moon inward, without requirin
science.content: New research suggests Venus may once have had a moon that spiraled inward and crashed into the planet because Venus rotates exceptionally slowly. Computer simulations led by University of California, Riverside astrophysicist Stephen Kane found that Venus's gravity and rotation could pull a moon inward, without requiring a later catastrophic impact to destroy it. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal on September 16, 2026. The findings offer an alternative to earlier explanations that Venus either never formed a moon or lost one in a massive impact. Outcomes varied depending on the moon's characteristics: some scenarios ended in a collision within about 30 million years, while others lasted as long as 1.7 billion years. The researchers describe the moon's existence as a possibility rather than an established historical fact.
science.image_alt: Venus may have swallowed a moon because of slow rotation

science.title: WMO finds 2025 among the driest years for global rivers
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization said Thursday that rivers worldwide experienced one of their driest years in more than three decades in 2025. Freshwater stored in groundwater, lakes, rivers, soil, vegetation, snow and ice was 42% below normal globally. Only about one-third of rivers had flows within their normal
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization said Thursday that rivers worldwide experienced one of their driest years in more than three decades in 2025. Freshwater stored in groundwater, lakes, rivers, soil, vegetation, snow and ice was 42% below normal globally. Only about one-third of rivers had flows within their normal range, while 36% of global river-basin area recorded below- or far-below-normal flows. The WMO attributed the increasingly erratic water cycle to climate-driven extreme weather, including glacier melt, severe drought and flash flooding. It said the past seven years had the fewest rivers with normal flows since 1991 and warned that declining land-based water storage has reduced reserves that can buffer dry periods.
science.image_alt: WMO finds 2025 among the driest years for global rivers

science.title: Satellite study finds 11.3 trillion tonnes of polar ice lost
science.summary: Greenland and Antarctica lost about 11.3 trillion metric tons of ice between 1979 and 2023, raising global sea levels by 3.14 centimeters, according to a study published in Scientific Data. The analysis draws on the longest satellite record assembled for the two ice sheets and was conducted by the international Ice She
science.content: Greenland and Antarctica lost about 11.3 trillion metric tons of ice between 1979 and 2023, raising global sea levels by 3.14 centimeters, according to a study published in Scientific Data. The analysis draws on the longest satellite record assembled for the two ice sheets and was conducted by the international Ice Sheet Mass Balance Intercomparison Exercise, with support from NASA and the European Space Agency. About five-sixths of the loss stemmed from processes other than warmer air. Warmer water eroded ice from below and along the margins, while glaciers accelerated and discharged more ice into the ocean rather than losing mass only through surface melting. Greenland accounted for about 60% of the documented loss and Antarctica 40%, and the two ice sheets now contribute roughly one-quarter of global sea-level rise.
science.image_alt: Satellite study finds 11.3 trillion tonnes of polar ice lost

science.title: Researchers solve 1848 solar storm train-delay mystery
science.summary: An international research team has solved a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a 16-minute train delay in Exeter in 1848, identifying it as one of the earliest recorded examples of space weather affecting human technology. The disruption occurred on the Victorian railway system during a solar storm, according to reports
science.content: An international research team has solved a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a 16-minute train delay in Exeter in 1848, identifying it as one of the earliest recorded examples of space weather affecting human technology. The disruption occurred on the Victorian railway system during a solar storm, according to reports on the study. Lancaster University led the research, which used historical records to reconstruct how solar activity disrupted 19th-century railway technology.
science.image_alt: Researchers solve 1848 solar storm train-delay mystery

science.title: Spanish scientists identify first European Diplodocus fossils
science.summary: Spanish paleontologists have identified fossils from El Castellar in Teruel, eastern Spain, as belonging to the genus Diplodocus, the first evidence that the long-necked dinosaur lived outside North America. The fossils include 14 caudal vertebrae and several chevron bones from sediments dating to about 150 million yea
science.content: Spanish paleontologists have identified fossils from El Castellar in Teruel, eastern Spain, as belonging to the genus Diplodocus, the first evidence that the long-necked dinosaur lived outside North America. The fossils include 14 caudal vertebrae and several chevron bones from sediments dating to about 150 million years ago, according to research published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology. Alberto Cobos, the foundation's managing director and a study co-author, estimated that the animal was about 25 metres long.
science.image_alt: Spanish scientists identify first European Diplodocus fossils

science.title: Chimpanzee mothers demonstrate tool use to infants in Senegal
science.summary: Researchers studying western chimpanzees in Senegal recorded adults demonstrating tool-use behaviors before transferring sticks or food to infants, which then copied the actions. The footage documents two apparent teaching episodes involving a mother and a juvenile male; researchers said both infants successfully repro
science.content: Researchers studying western chimpanzees in Senegal recorded adults demonstrating tool-use behaviors before transferring sticks or food to infants, which then copied the actions. The footage documents two apparent teaching episodes involving a mother and a juvenile male; researchers said both infants successfully reproduced the demonstrated behavior. The observations were made in the Dindefelo reserve between 2017 and 2025. The study, published in Frontiers in Psychology, examines 33 instances of chimpanzees passing tools to one another. Transfers usually occurred between relatives, particularly mothers and immature offspring. Researchers said receiving tools and food may help young chimpanzees learn techniques for extracting difficult-to-access foods.
science.image_alt: Chimpanzee mothers demonstrate tool use to infants in Senegal

science.title: James Webb reveals star-forming cloud and brown dwarfs
science.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured a detailed infrared image of IC 348, a star-forming region about 1,000 light-years away in the constellation Perseus. The image shows dense molecular clouds and bright young stars. The region is also used to search for brown dwarfs, objects that form through the collapse of m
science.content: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured a detailed infrared image of IC 348, a star-forming region about 1,000 light-years away in the constellation Perseus. The image shows dense molecular clouds and bright young stars. The region is also used to search for brown dwarfs, objects that form through the collapse of molecular clouds but lack enough mass to sustain hydrogen fusion. The smallest known stars have about 8% of the Sun’s mass, while objects below that threshold are classified as brown dwarfs. Researchers continue to investigate how small objects formed through cloud collapse can become.
science.image_alt: James Webb reveals star-forming cloud and brown dwarfs

science.title: Hottest U.S. summer on record followed by September heat dome
science.summary: Meteorological summer 2026 was the hottest on record for the contiguous United States, surpassing records from 1936 and 2021 by 0.4 degrees Fahrenheit. The June-August average was 3 degrees Fahrenheit above the 20th-century average, while August was 3.5 degrees above average. NOAA confirmed the record, and a Climate Ce
science.content: Meteorological summer 2026 was the hottest on record for the contiguous United States, surpassing records from 1936 and 2021 by 0.4 degrees Fahrenheit. The June-August average was 3 degrees Fahrenheit above the 20th-century average, while August was 3.5 degrees above average. NOAA confirmed the record, and a Climate Central analysis found that 293 million Americans, or 86% of the population, experienced at least 30 days of unusually risky heat. Heat persisted into mid-September as a high-pressure system formed a heat dome over the south-central United States. NASA said temperatures approached or exceeded 40 degrees Celsius in parts of the region on September 15, while more than 41 million Americans were under extreme-heat advisories, watches or warnings. Meteorologists reported repeated 100-degree days in cities including Dallas, Oklahoma City and Wichita and said the dome expanded, shifted and re-intensified several times.
science.image_alt: Hottest U.S. summer on record followed by September heat dome

sports.title: Liverpool youngster Koumas earns praise after Spurs cup win
sports.summary: Lewis Koumas delivered an energetic performance as Liverpool beat Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 at Anfield on September 15 to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round. The 20-year-old academy graduate led the line, pressed consistently and earned Liverpool’s Player of the Match award. Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szob
sports.content: Lewis Koumas delivered an energetic performance as Liverpool beat Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 at Anfield on September 15 to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round. The 20-year-old academy graduate led the line, pressed consistently and earned Liverpool’s Player of the Match award. Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai scored for the hosts. Koumas said the opportunity reflected manager Andoni Iraola’s trust in his tactical work, particularly away from the ball. The display followed Iraola’s call for greater pressing and tenacity from Liverpool’s forwards after a poor league draw with Fulham. Koumas made his second senior Liverpool start and played 86 minutes, according to WalesOnline.
sports.image_alt: Liverpool youngster Koumas earns praise after Spurs cup win

sports.title: Manchester United opens talks to keep teenager JJ Gabriel
sports.summary: Manchester United is trying to persuade 15-year-old academy forward JJ Gabriel to stay after he formally asked to cancel his registration and leave the club. Chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe are involved in the talks. Gabriel had been expected to join United
sports.content: Manchester United is trying to persuade 15-year-old academy forward JJ Gabriel to stay after he formally asked to cancel his registration and leave the club. Chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe are involved in the talks. Gabriel had been expected to join United’s senior squad for the Carabao Cup match against Brighton but was not selected after his request became public. He has attracted interest from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Manchester City, with reports identifying Barcelona and Real Madrid as leading contenders.
sports.image_alt: Manchester United opens talks to keep teenager JJ Gabriel

sports.title: Max Verstappen beats 100 karters in Silverstone challenge
sports.summary: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen won Red Bull’s “Max vs 100” exhibition at Silverstone on September 16, starting 101st and overtaking all 100 amateur competitors in 14 laps and about 35 minutes. The adapted circuit featured content creators, athletes, journalists and fans, with each driver eliminated o
sports.content: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen won Red Bull’s “Max vs 100” exhibition at Silverstone on September 16, starting 101st and overtaking all 100 amateur competitors in 14 laps and about 35 minutes. The adapted circuit featured content creators, athletes, journalists and fans, with each driver eliminated once Verstappen passed them. He finished well inside the event’s 75-minute limit. Multiple crashes and spins on the opening lap led to a brief race suspension, but Verstappen climbed to 37th almost immediately and reached the top 10 by lap six. The final three drivers—journalist Jacky Martens, Red Bull engine builder Lewis Osler and YouTuber Zac Alsop—received additional shortcut opportunities, but Verstappen passed all three to win.
sports.image_alt: Max Verstappen beats 100 karters in Silverstone challenge

sports.title: McIlroy shoots 12-under 60 in BMW PGA Championship pro-am
sports.summary: Rory McIlroy shot a 12-under-par 60 in Wednesday’s BMW PGA Championship Celebrity Pro-Am at Wentworth Club in Surrey, ahead of the DP World Tour event’s start on Thursday, September 17. The world No. 2 is seeking a strong result after a season in which he won the Masters for a second consecutive year and completed the
sports.content: Rory McIlroy shot a 12-under-par 60 in Wednesday’s BMW PGA Championship Celebrity Pro-Am at Wentworth Club in Surrey, ahead of the DP World Tour event’s start on Thursday, September 17. The world No. 2 is seeking a strong result after a season in which he won the Masters for a second consecutive year and completed the career Grand Slam. The tournament includes many of Europe’s leading Ryder Cup players, including Jon Rahm, Shane Lowry, Tommy Fleetwood, Tyrrell Hatton, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ludvig Åberg, Viktor Hovland, Justin Rose and Robert MacIntyre. The Celebrity Pro-Am also included former footballers Gareth Bale, John Terry and Eden Hazard.
sports.image_alt: McIlroy shoots 12-under 60 in BMW PGA Championship pro-am

sports.title: Tottenham face mounting pressure after Liverpool cup defeat

sports.content: Tottenham Hotspur lost 3-1 to Liverpool at Anfield on Tuesday, September 15, in the Carabao Cup third round. Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai scored for Liverpool, while Conor Gallagher’s 69th-minute header gave Spurs their first goal against Premier League opposition this season. Roberto De Zerbi apologised to supporters and said Tottenham were in a “tough moment” after the defeat. Spurs have taken two points from their first four Premier League matches, with two draws and two losses, and remain without a league win; their only victory this season came against Championship club Charlton in the previous League Cup round. The manager said the team must improve both the number and quality of its shots before hosting Aston Villa in its next match.

sports.content: Formula 1 and the FIA have approved a 2027 calendar with 24 Grands Prix in 22 countries and a record 10 Sprint weekends, up from six in 2026. The season is set to begin in Bahrain on March 12–14, following four days of pre-season testing at the same circuit from February 24–27, and end in Abu Dhabi on December 10–12. Monaco will host a Sprint for the first time, alongside first-time Sprint venues Bahrain, Australia, Japan and Abu Dhabi; Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil and Qatar retain or regain the format. Portugal returns at Portimão on June 18–20 and Türkiye returns at Istanbul Park on October 1–3, while Zandvoort leaves the schedule and Barcelona will not race in 2027 under its alternating arrangement with Spa-Francorchamps. Formula 1 expanded the Sprint programme, citing strong demand and higher engagement. The planned events in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi remain subject to regional security conditions after 2026 races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were disrupted or cancelled.

sports.content: Barcelona defeated Racing Santander 7-2 at Camp Nou on September 16 to extend their perfect start to seven competitive wins, the best in club history. Raphinha scored a hat-trick, including two penalties, while João Cancelo, Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored. Asier Villalibre added an own goal for the hosts. Maguette Gueye and Yassir Zabiri scored for Racing. The victory kept Barcelona three points ahead of Real Madrid at the top of La Liga after six league matches. Hansi Flick’s team has scored 33 goals in seven matches across all competitions, including 28 in the league.

sports.content: Inter Miami defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 at Nu Stadium in Miami on Wednesday, September 16, to win the Campeones Cup for the first time. Lionel Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in Luis Suárez’s cross to reach 100 goals for Inter Miami in his 115th appearance across all competitions. Casemiro sealed the victory in the 81st minute by heading in Messi’s corner. The match pitted the reigning MLS Cup champion against the winner of Mexico’s Liga MX championship series. It also marked Cristian “Kily” González’s first match as Inter Miami manager and was Miami’s first trophy at Nu Stadium since the venue opened in April 2026. The result ended a run of three consecutive Campeones Cup victories by Mexican clubs.
